title: Yet something of sin remains; even Rome must grant this
source_text: XXVI. Quod autem nihilominus contendimus per Christi gratiam peccatum non sic tolli & aboleri, quin aliquid peccati, dum hanc vitam vivimus, in ipsis fidelibus & justificatis supersit: cujus ratione semper Dei misericordia & gratia egeant, prout supra fuit a nobis expositum; res ita certa & explorata est, ut ipsi Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae cogantur ei dare manus, & veritati illius subscribere.
pass_a_gloss: But that we nevertheless contend that through Christ's grace sin is not so taken away and abolished that something of sin does not remain, while we live this life, in the faithful and justified themselves—on account of which they always need God's mercy and grace, as was explained by us above—is a matter so certain and explored that the Doctors of the Roman Church themselves are compelled to give it their hand and subscribe to its truth.
pass_b_english: We still hold that in this life some sin remains in the justified, who always need mercy.
Even Roman doctors are forced to grant that explored truth.
